title: Strategies to increase uptake of bereavement follow-up offered by palliative care services: a rapid review
abstract: Background: uptake of bereavement follow-up offered by palliative care services is low and unequal. Aim: to update a 2023 systematic review and summarise strategies associated with higher uptake. Methods: rapid review with declared shortcuts, searching from January 2022, grouping studies by strategy and reporting uptake as accepting an offer and as attending at least one session. Results and conclusions will be written after the review is complete.
introduction: Bereaved relatives are offered follow-up by most palliative care services, yet few take it up, and uptake is lowest among men, relatives who need an interpreter and relatives living far away. A 2023 review found proactive personal contact the most consistent signal but searched only to March 2022.
methods: Three databases and two grey-literature sources searched from January 2022 to October 2026, plus the studies in the 2023 review. Single-reviewer screening with independent screening of a random 20 percent; extraction checked for every uptake figure; synthesis without meta-analysis by strategy; certainty per strategy with GRADE.
results: No review data have been extracted yet. The report will present the study flow, a table of strategies with uptake by definition, an effect direction plot, and results for men, relatives who need an interpreter and relatives living far away.
discussion: The discussion will state which strategies have evidence of higher uptake, how certain it is, which groups remain unstudied, and what the hospice will change and evaluate.
limitations: Rapid review shortcuts; English-language reports only; mostly before-after service evaluations; uptake defined in different ways.
conclusion: To be written after the review; it will be limited to uptake and will not claim effects on grief outcomes that no study measured adequately.
reportingChecklist: PRISMA 2020 with rapid review shortcuts reported; SWiM
summary: PRISMA-structured rapid review draft with results left empty until extraction is complete.
